tagline: Up the White River, over the crest, down to the orchards.
intro: Enumclaw sits on a plateau laid down by a mudflow off Mount Rainier. Out of town, SR 410 follows the White River upstream through old-growth forest and into the national park. At Cayuse Pass it turns east and climbs a run of hairpins past Tipsoo Lake to Chinook Pass, 5,430 feet and above the trees. Then it comes down along the American and Naches rivers to Naches.

The road was built from both ends, the east side with horse teams and, after 1924, an army tractor, and the halves met at Tipsoo Lake in 1931. The lower Naches Pass needed a tunnel and lost on cost. No highway has crossed it yet.

moments.title: Federation Forest State Park
moments.text: The state's women's clubs bought their first old-growth park near Snoqualmie Pass and lost it to windstorms and logging. This stand on the White River, dedicated in 1949, is the second try.

moments.title: Chinook Pass
moments.text: On the Cascade crest above the treeline, the Pacific Crest Trail crosses the road, and in winter the snow at the summit can lie fifteen feet deep.

moments.title: Naches
moments.text: The byway ends at US 12 in a town of about 1,100 on the Naches River that lives on timber and on apples, cherries and pears.

practical: Chinook Pass usually closes in November and reopens around mid-May, with a winter gate at Morse Creek about five miles east of the summit. Commercial vehicles are not allowed on the national park section.

sources.label: State of Washington Tourism, Chinook Scenic Byway
